hunks.baseline: But if you’d spent all four days riding hard, barely stopping to rest and catching only snatches of sleep in the saddle, that was another matter.
hunks.sol: But if you’d spent all four days riding hard, barely stopping to rest and catching snatches of sleep in the saddle, that was another matter.

hunks.baseline: Jin Taekyung had left them with those words, then gone off to a meeting with the leadership. The Fire Dragon Pavilion members he’d left behind had faithfully followed their Pavilion Master’s orders.
hunks.sol: Jin Taekyung had left them with those words, then gone off to a meeting with the leadership. The Fire Dragon Pavilion members he’d left behind had followed their Pavilion Master’s orders to the letter.

hunks.baseline: And so, now, they’d unpacked their few belongings, finished bathing in warm water, and settled in before a sumptuous feast that had somehow already been laid out.
hunks.sol: Now they’d unpacked their few belongings, bathed in warm water, and settled before a sumptuous feast that had somehow already been laid out.

hunks.baseline: The Fire King was a towering figure of his generation. He needed no explanation. And the title of Young Sect Leader of the Black Dragon Demon Gate placed Sama Pyo well within the ranks of the leadership.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang was the Fire King, a giant of his generation. His place at the meeting needed no explanation. And as Young Sect Leader of the Black Dragon Demon Gate, Sama Pyo belonged among the leadership too.

hunks.baseline: Ju Hwaran’s words might as well have spoken for every member of the Fire Dragon Pavilion.
hunks.sol: Ju Hwaran spoke for every member of the Fire Dragon Pavilion.

hunks.baseline: Physical exhaustion was bad enough, but mental fatigue squeezed at the body and mind in a way that put it to shame.
hunks.sol: Physical exhaustion was bad enough, but mental fatigue weighed on both body and mind far more heavily.

hunks.baseline: For a martial artist, crossing the line between life and death was a lifelong fate. The grief and pain brought on by war were the lot of those living through troubled times.
hunks.sol: For a martial artist, passing through the jaws of death was a lifelong fate. The grief and pain of war were the lot of those living through troubled times.

hunks.baseline: At least everyone in the Fire Dragon Pavilion understood their circumstances clearly—and had accepted them.
hunks.sol: At least everyone in the Fire Dragon Pavilion understood their circumstances—and had accepted them.

hunks.baseline: “Our Pavilion Master was right. We have to rest as much as we can while we have the time if we’re to prepare for what comes next. With that in mind, let’s eat.”
hunks.sol: “Our Pavilion Master was right. We have to rest as much as we can while there’s time, so we’re ready for what comes next. With that in mind, let’s eat.”

hunks.baseline: Perhaps the bump sticking out of the crown of his head was bothering him. With the conversation interrupted, Hyuk Mujin took the opportunity to rub it, then buried his face in his plate again.
hunks.sol: Perhaps the bump on the crown of his head was bothering him. Now that he’d paused, Hyuk Mujin took the opportunity to rub it, then buried his face in his plate again.

hunks.baseline: A moment later, he looked up and stared intently at Song Ilseom.
hunks.sol: A moment later, he looked up and stared at Song Ilseom.

hunks.baseline: Gulp.
hunks.sol: *Gulp.*

hunks.baseline: The longer the conversation went on, the worse things seemed to get for Hyuk Mujin.
hunks.sol: The longer the conversation went on, the worse things got for Hyuk Mujin.

hunks.baseline: His eyes rolled around as he searched for a counterargument. Then an idea came to him.
hunks.sol: His eyes darted about as he searched for a counterargument. Then an idea came to him.

hunks.baseline: “Hey, what do you mean, ‘So?’ You use at least a polite form of speech with the Captain. Why do you get to talk down to me—”
hunks.sol: “Hey, what do you mean, ‘So?’ You speak at least somewhat politely to the Captain. Why do you get to talk down to me—”

hunks.baseline: As Hyuk Mujin blinked at Song Ilseom’s absurdly confident attitude, he suddenly felt anger rising from deep in his chest.
hunks.sol: As Hyuk Mujin blinked at Song Ilseom’s absurdly confident expression, anger rose from deep in his chest.

hunks.baseline: He could put up with Jin Taekyung giving him a hard time whenever he got the chance. That much he could gladly accept as the loyal right hand and self-proclaimed heart of his Captain.
hunks.sol: He could put up with Jin Taekyung giving him a hard time whenever he got the chance. That much he could gladly accept as his Captain’s loyal right hand and self-proclaimed heart.

hunks.baseline: But now he was being treated this way even by Song Ilseom—a lowly wandering martial artist who’d joined them along the way. Sure, for a mere wanderer, he was famous as hell in those circles, and, as it turned out, he came from an impressive martial family. But still!
hunks.sol: But now he was getting the same treatment from Song Ilseom—a mere wandering martial artist who’d joined them along the way. Sure, Song Ilseom was famous as hell among wanderers, and, as it turned out, he came from an impressive martial family. But still!

hunks.baseline: A fire lit in Hyuk Mujin’s eyes as he glared at Song Ilseom. The roasted chicken leg in his hand, which he’d been clutching for a while, trembled as though it were a sword resonating with its wielder.
hunks.sol: Fire lit in Hyuk Mujin’s eyes as he glared at Song Ilseom. The roasted chicken leg he’d been holding trembled like a sword resonating with its wielder.

hunks.baseline: “What? Got something to say? Then say it quickly. I’m hungry, and I don’t want the precious food to get cold.”
hunks.sol: “What? Got something to say? Then say it quickly. I’m hungry, and I don’t want this precious food to get cold.”

hunks.baseline: How could anyone be so shameless about being such a coward?
hunks.sol: How could anyone be so brazen about being a coward?

hunks.baseline: “They’re kind, simple people. Thanks for the compliment.”
hunks.sol: “They’re simple, good-hearted people. Thanks for the compliment.”

hunks.baseline: They’d been told to rest and take it easy, but who would look at that and think they were about to go into battle?
hunks.sol: They’d been told to rest and take it easy, but who would look at them and think they were about to go into battle?

hunks.baseline: They looked more like a pack of beggars come to bankrupt an inn.
hunks.sol: A pack of beggars come to bankrupt an inn, maybe.

hunks.baseline: Song Ilseom had spent years among wandering martial artists—a crowd of crazies so thick you could hardly turn around without running into one. But the people he’d been with for the past year or so were strange from top to bottom.
hunks.sol: Song Ilseom had spent years among wandering martial artists, where crazies were everywhere. But the people he’d been with for the past year or so were strange from top to bottom.

hunks.baseline: The degree of it was on another level from anything he’d seen before.
hunks.sol: They were on another level from any madman he’d met before.

hunks.baseline: No words were needed. The proof was how Song Ilseom’s breath caught just thinking about him.
hunks.sol: No words were needed. Just thinking about him made Song Ilseom’s breath catch.

hunks.baseline: Watching Jeok Cheongang up close had driven one point home once again: the law of the jungle still ruled the world.
hunks.sol: Watching Jeok Cheongang up close had driven one point home once again: the law of the strong devouring the weak still ruled this world.

hunks.baseline: *If it didn’t, Jeok Cheongang would have been dead several times over by now.*
hunks.sol: *Otherwise, he’d have been dead several times over by now.*

hunks.baseline: Why did he think that?
hunks.sol: Why did Song Ilseom think that?

hunks.baseline: If they belonged to the orthodox faction, he’d dig into their hearts with a tongue sharper than a famous sword. If they were from the unorthodox faction or the dark-path underworld, he’d immediately size them up for a punch. As for fiends, he’d once said:
hunks.sol: If they belonged to the orthodox faction, he’d cut them to the heart with a tongue sharper than a famous sword. If they were from the unorthodox faction or were dark-path figures, he’d look for an opening to throw a punch. As for fiends, he’d once said:

hunks.baseline: > *“I may as well tell you now: for many years, my fondest wish has been to reform every fiend beneath heaven and make them good.”*
hunks.sol: > *“I may as well tell you now: for many years, this old man’s wish has been to reform every fiend beneath heaven and make them good.”*

hunks.baseline: What else could explain his one and only Disciple saying this about his own Master?
hunks.sol: Why else would his one and only Disciple say this about his own Master?

hunks.baseline: Sometimes, for reasons known only to him, he’d act like a perfectly normal person. But when something rubbed him the wrong way, he could show a side that even surpassed his Master, Jeok Cheongang.
hunks.sol: Sometimes, for reasons known only to him, he’d act like a perfectly normal person. But when something rubbed him the wrong way, he could outdo even his Master, Jeok Cheongang.

hunks.baseline: Even if Jeok Cheongang cursed him with every filthy word in the world until he feared qi deviation, even if his Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist crushed Song Ilseom’s Eight Extraordinary Meridians, Jeok Cheongang would still be preferable.
hunks.sol: Even if Jeok Cheongang cursed him with every filthy word he knew until Song Ilseom feared qi deviation, even if his Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist crushed Song Ilseom’s Eight Extraordinary Meridians, Jeok Cheongang would still be preferable.

hunks.baseline: Just remembering him made Song Ilseom’s stomach churn.
hunks.sol: Just thinking about him made Song Ilseom’s stomach churn.

hunks.baseline: His martial prowess, now so far beyond Song Ilseom’s reach, was one thing. But his reputation for surpassing his Master in the art of verbal abuse was a nightmare all on its own.
hunks.sol: His martial prowess, now so far beyond Song Ilseom’s reach, was one thing. But his tongue, widely held to have surpassed even his Master’s, was the stuff of nightmares.

hunks.baseline: The one small comfort was that his terrifying tongue always seemed to work at full strength only against enemies.
hunks.sol: The one small comfort was that his terrifying tongue only ever seemed to show its full power against enemies.

hunks.baseline: And even aside from that, Song Ilseom was one of the people who got the least grief from Jin Taekyung, along with Sama Pyo and Ju Hwaran.
hunks.sol: Even aside from that, Song Ilseom was among those who got the least grief from Jin Taekyung, along with Sama Pyo and Ju Hwaran.

hunks.baseline: With a low hum, Song Ilseom came back to himself from his deep thoughts.
hunks.sol: With that unconscious murmur, Song Ilseom surfaced from his thoughts.

hunks.baseline: It wasn’t a question directed at anyone in particular. It was closer to a disbelieving gasp.
hunks.sol: It wasn’t a question directed at anyone in particular. It was closer to an exclamation of shock.

hunks.baseline: Song Ilseom stood frozen, eyes wide. Ju Hwaran and Hyuk Mujin, both wearing serious expressions, answered in turn.
hunks.sol: Song Ilseom sat frozen, eyes wide. Ju Hwaran and Hyuk Mujin, both wearing serious expressions, answered in turn.

hunks.baseline: “We don’t know either. What happened?”
hunks.sol: “We don’t know either. How did this happen?”

hunks.baseline: Pth, pth!
hunks.sol: *Pth, pth!*

hunks.baseline: Usually, Song Ilseom would have dodged the spray of food with a quick sidestep. This time, he couldn’t.
hunks.sol: Ordinarily, Song Ilseom would have dodged the spray of food with a quick movement. This time, he couldn’t.

hunks.baseline: Splut!
hunks.sol: *Splut!*

hunks.baseline: Something unpleasant touched his skin.
hunks.sol: Something unpleasant struck his skin.

hunks.baseline: Hyuk Mujin froze, worried about what he’d done. But despite his fears, Song Ilseom didn’t move.
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin froze, worried about what he’d done. But despite his fears, Song Ilseom didn’t react.

hunks.baseline: He could only stare at one person, stunned as if he’d come face-to-face with a living dragon.
hunks.sol: He could only stare at one person, as stunned as if he’d come face-to-face with a living dragon.

hunks.baseline: Taishan was sitting before a feast fit for a king, yet his shoulders drooped and he didn’t move at all.
hunks.sol: Taishan sat before a mouthwatering feast, his shoulders drooping, without moving a muscle.

hunks.baseline: Just as those disbelieving words slipped from someone’s lips—
hunks.sol: The disbelieving words had barely left someone’s lips when another voice answered.

hunks.baseline: The voice was quiet and low.
hunks.sol: The voice was low and subdued.

hunks.baseline: Namho, who’d been sitting motionless from the start, lost in thought, twitched his nose.
hunks.sol: Namho, who’d sat motionless and lost in thought all this time, twitched his nose.

hunks.baseline: As if he were following the scent of a memory from a day not so long ago.
hunks.sol: As if trying to catch a scent he remembered from a day not so long ago.
